notes: Cliopatria row: Southern Yan 402..409 (two identical shapes of 152,855 km2). (1) The state lives 398-410; Cliopatria has the Shandong shape from 402 and nothing for Huatai in 398-399, and ends one year early (the Western Jin shape takes the land in 410). (2) Dates inside the page disagree: the infobox puts 'Capture of Guanggu' in 399 while the text has De attack Qing Province after Fu Guang's rebellion in 399 and become emperor in 400; both are treated as 399. (3) The page has Chao agree to become a Later Qin vassal in 407 (Later Qin's dossier holds that relation, vassal_start 407 and vassal_end 410) and gives no month for Linqu or the siege. (4) Huatai and Guanggu locations are the researcher's readings; no commanderies are named, so the Shandong edge is Cliopatria's. (5) Counterparts: Northern Wei took Huatai in 399. Gazetteer names needed: Huatai (place, Hua County, Henan) and Guanggu (place, near Qingzhou, Shandong). Cross-dossier gaps: the Western Jin dossier has no 399 loss of Qing Province to the Southern Yan (it gains the Shandong from the Southern Yan in 410), and the Northern Wei dossier has no 399 gain of Huatai from the Southern Yan. Page budget: two pages.
